name: Croatia
summary: Red, white and blue horizontal bands with the Croatian coat of arms: a red and white chequerboard topped by a crown of five small shields. The tricolour dates from 1848.
origin: Red, white and blue were adopted as Croatian colours during the revolutions of 1848, combining the red and white of Croatia with the blue of Dalmatia and Slavonia, and reflecting the Pan-Slavic colours.

The chequerboard (šahovnica) has been a Croatian symbol since at least the late 15th century. After the first multi-party elections in 1990, Croatia adopted the tricolour with a new coat of arms designed by Miroslav Šutej on 21 December 1990.

symbols.name: Chequerboard (šahovnica)
symbols.description: A shield of 25 red and white squares, starting with red in the top left.
symbols.meaning: Croatia; its origin is uncertain, with legends linking it to a medieval king playing chess.

symbols.name: Crown of five shields
symbols.description: Five small shields above the chequerboard.
symbols.meaning: Croatia's historical regions: the oldest Croatian arms, Dubrovnik, Dalmatia, Istria and Slavonia.

facts: Croatia's national football kit uses the red and white chequerboard pattern.
The coat of arms on the flag slightly overlaps the red and blue bands.
The Netherlands and Russia use the same colours; Croatia's arms tell them apart.

Its national football kit copies the shield's pattern.
